# BluePaper

> BluePaper is a document sanitizer from Bluethroat Labs. Upload an untrusted document and receive a PDF rebuilt from pixels, plus a report of raw byte indicators found in the original. Safety comes from destruction, not detection.

BluePaper is a network-service fork of Dangerzone (Freedom of the Press Foundation), licensed under AGPL-3.0. The original file is opened only inside a fresh, hardware-isolated, network-denied Azure Container Apps sandbox, which renders each page to raw pixels and is then deleted. A trusted worker builds a new PDF from those pixels, with an optional OCR text layer. In parallel, a parser-free scan lists raw byte indicators in the original, such as /JavaScript, /OpenAction, /Launch, vbaProject.bin, and DDE markers.

Supported inputs: PDF; Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; OpenDocument; Hancom HWP and HWPX; EPUB; and common images. Uploads are typically limited to 32 MiB.

Important limitations:

- BluePaper is not a malware scanner. It never labels a file malicious or clean.
- Zero regexp hits is not "clean". Compression and encodings can hide indicators.
- A hit is not proof that an active construct was present. The same bytes can occur in inert data.
- A failed conversion produces no safe PDF and is not a malware verdict. Do not open the original as a fallback.
- The safe PDF keeps everything visible on the page, including phishing text, links, and QR codes. Links, form fields, attachments, and digital signatures are not preserved.
- The web console requires a human check (Cloudflare Turnstile). Agents must not automate it. Programmatic access uses the REST API with an operator-issued API key.
- The uploaded original is stored under its SHA-256 hash in the operator's storage. Delete removes the safe PDF, report, and job record, but not the original. Do not upload material you are not authorized to share.
